newsitem.title: UK: BPB profit up, accounts change halves stg hit.
newsitem.headline: BPB profit up, accounts change halves stg hit.

text.p: British building materials group BPB Industries Plc notched up year pretax profits above market expectations on Thursday, buttressed by disposal proceeds and a change in accounting policy to reduce the impact of the soaring pound.

Pretax profits for the group were 189.1 million pounds ($314.4 million) in the year ended March 31, versus 161.4 million the previous year. The headline profit figure reflected a change in accounting for the translational impact of currencies, with BPB changing its policy to use an average exchange rate instead of a closing rate. This halved the hit from sterling strength to 10 million pounds as a result.
Profits under the old accounting basis of using year-end exchange rates were 178.3 million pounds, versus 161.1 million -- better than the forecast range of 160 to 165 million pounds.
Current trading prospects for the group were reported as mixed, with sterling strength against the German mark continuing to cause concern.

"The current year will see conflicting forces at work. Further progress is expected in building materials but offsetting this will be the slow pace of recovery by the paperboard division and further adverse translation effects on overseas earnings from the continuing strength of sterling," said the BPB statement.
Group sales last year fell 2.8 percent to 1.39 billion pounds from 1.42 billion the previous year at average exchange rate terms, although in local market currency terms sales had risen slightly.

Building materials showed a 7.8 percent rise in profits last year to 152.6 million pounds on sales growth of 5.8 percent in local currency terms. Plasterboard sales were up eight percent, with margins improving by one percent.
But the paperboard unit suffered a second half reversal in profitability as selling prices fell faster than input costs for recycled fibre. Profits there fell by a quarter to 13.4 million pounds.
